gaps.sentence: She ___ her breath before diving into the pool.
gaps.explanation: 'Hold one's breath' — catching breath is recovering it afterwards.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ your seats; the performance is about to begin.
gaps.explanation: take your seats is the formal way of asking people to sit down.

gaps.sentence: The editors decided to ___ the chapter from the paperback edition.
gaps.explanation: "Omit" = leave out; the other -mit verbs mean let in, hand in, or send (money).

gaps.sentence: The manager ___ an announcement about the changes yesterday.
gaps.explanation: make an announcement is the fixed collocation for stating something publicly.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ your word, people will trust you.
gaps.explanation: keep your word means to do what you promised.

gaps.sentence: She ___ no difficulty finding the address.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ no difficulty doing something
gaps.explanation: have no difficulty (in) doing something is the fixed pattern; 'made no difficulty' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: She ___ attention to every detail of the contract.
The children ___ great fun at the fair.
